summary: Three nouns share this spelling. אֵם is mother: the woman who bears and nurses a child (Gen 3:20; 1Ki 3:27), the dam of a beast (Exo 22:29), and by figure a people or city that brings forth its members (Isa 50:1; Hos 2:4; 2Sa 20:19), the figure Paul takes up in “the Jerusalem above … is our mother” (Gal 4:26). אַמָּה is the cubit, the forearm’s length, the measure of the ark, the tabernacle, the temple and Ezekiel’s house (Gen 6:15; Deu 3:11; Ezk 40:5). אֻמָּה, rare in Hebrew and frequent in Daniel’s Aramaic, is a tribe or people, as in “peoples, nations and languages” (Gen 25:16; Psa 117:1; Dan 7:14). Arabic and Syriac set the people word beside the mother word, as a people born of one mother; how the cubit belongs with them is not known.

words.summary: The common measure of length, the forearm from elbow to fingertip, in the plural אַמּוֹת and the dual אַמָּתַיִם. The count of 249 by spelling includes three tokens that are not this word: Isa 6:4 (its own word, below), 2Sa 8:1 (מֶתֶג הָאַמָּה, a place name filed under another key) and 2Sa 2:24 (גִּבְעַת אַמָּה, the hill of Ammah). Akkadian ammatu is both “forearm” and “cubit”, as Syriac and the Targums’ Aramaic are “cubit”; how this word belongs with אֵם “mother” and אֻמָּה “people” is not understood, and Akkadian keeps ammatu and ummu apart.

senses.definition: A measure of length taken from a man’s forearm: the unit of the ark, the tabernacle and its vessels, Solomon’s house, Ezekiel’s temple and men’s stature. A longer cubit, “a cubit and a handbreadth”, is named for Ezekiel’s measuring and an older standard for Solomon’s temple.

evidence.note: “The length of the ark 300 אַמָּה, its width fifty אַמָּה, and its height thirty אַמָּה.”
Og’s couch “nine אַמּוֹת long and four אַמּוֹת wide, בְּאַמַּת אִישׁ”, by the cubit of a man: the measure taken from the body.
The measuring reed “six אַמּוֹת בָּאַמָּה וָטֹפַח”, in cubits of a cubit and a handbreadth.
“The measurements of the altar בָּאַמּוֹת: אַמָּה is אַמָּה וָטֹפַח.”
Solomon’s house: “the length in אַמּוֹת בַּמִּדָּה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה”, by the former measure, sixty cubits.
The ark of the covenant two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide and high.
Goliath’s height “שֵׁשׁ אַמּוֹת וָזָרֶת”, six cubits and a span.
“Fifteen אַמָּה upward the waters rose, and the mountains were covered.”
The Levites’ pasturelands a thousand cubits from the city wall.
“About two thousand אַמָּה בַּמִּדָּה” between the people and the ark.
Quails about two cubits deep on the face of the land.
The flying scroll twenty cubits long and ten wide.
The man with the line measures a thousand בָּאַמָּה, and the waters are ankle deep.
The new Jerusalem’s wall 144 cubits, “by the measure of a man, which is the angel’s”: the cubit still a man’s measure.

senses.definition: Once, the full measure of Babylon’s greed, set beside her end: the length allotted to her is reached.

evidence.note: “Dweller upon many waters, abundant in treasures, בָּא קִצֵּךְ אַמַּת בִּצְעֵךְ”: your end has come, the measure of your cutting off (or of your gain).

evidence.locator: Gen.6.15, אַמָּה → πήξεων; Deu.3.11, אַמּוֹת → πηξῶν, בְּאַמַּת → πήξει

evidence.note: “Which of you by being anxious can add one πῆχυν to his stature?”; the Peshitta has אַמתָֿא.
About two hundred cubits from land.
“144 πηχῶν, the measure of a man”, as Deu 3:11’s “cubit of a man”.

parallels.note: The span, the next smaller measure of the hand, added to cubits.
The handbreadth, which lengthens the cubit of Ezekiel’s temple.
The measuring reed of six cubits.
End, beside “the measure of your cutting off”.

phrases.gloss: by the cubit of a man, the common cubit
a cubit and a handbreadth, the long cubit

words.gloss: mother; dam; mother city or people; (once) parting of the way
words.summary: About 220 times, in every part of scripture, nearly always with a pronoun (“his mother”, “my mother”). The mother bears, nurses, teaches and comforts, and with the father is to be honoured. By figure a people, a city or a land is the mother of those born in it, and Israel the mother whom Yahweh put away for her transgressions. Every Semitic language has the same word, and Phoenician also calls a city “mother” of its colonies.

senses.definition: The woman who conceives, bears and nurses a child, set beside the father as the one who begot it; to be honoured, heard and not cursed. Her womb is where a man’s life begins and her house where a daughter returns.

evidence.note: Eve, “because she was אֵם כָּל חָי”, the mother of all the living.
Solomon’s judgment: “Give the living child to her … הִיא אִמּוֹ”, she is his mother.
“You and אִמְּךָ אֲשֶׁר יְלָדַתְךָ”, your mother who bore you.
אִמָּם beside הוֹרָתָם, “she who conceived them”.
“A man will leave his father and אִמּוֹ and cling to his wife”: quoted in Mat 19:5 and Eph 5:31.
“Honour your father and אִמֶּךָ”: quoted in Mat 15:4 and Eph 6:2.
Whoever curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.
“She is your mother; you shall not uncover her nakedness.”
“Do not forsake תּוֹרַת אִמֶּךָ”, the teaching of your mother.
A foolish son is the grief of his mother.
“As a man whom his mother comforts, so I will comfort you”: Yahweh’s comfort likened to a mother’s.
A soul quieted “like a weaned child upon his mother”.
“Naked I came from בֶּטֶן אִמִּי.”
“You knit me together בְּבֶטֶן אִמִּי.”
“Return, each woman to the house of her mother.”
“My father and my mother have left me, but Yahweh will take me up.”

senses.definition: In Judah the king’s mother had a place at court beside him, and the books of Kings name her at each king’s accession.

evidence.note: Solomon “set a throne לְאֵם הַמֶּלֶךְ, and she sat at his right hand”.
Asa removed Maacah אִמּוֹ from being queen mother (גְּבִירָה) for her Asherah.
“וְשֵׁם אִמּוֹ נַעֲמָה הָעַמֹּנִית”: the formula at each accession.
Jehoiachin exiled with אֵם הַמֶּלֶךְ.

senses.gloss: dam, mother of a beast or bird
senses.definition: The mother of a young animal or bird, which the law protects: the young stays seven days with its mother, a kid is not boiled in its mother’s milk, and the mother bird is let go.

evidence.note: The firstborn of ox and sheep: “seven days it will be עִם אִמּוֹ”.
“Seven days תַּחַת אִמּוֹ.”
“You shall not boil a kid בַּחֲלֵב אִמּוֹ.”
“And הָאֵם sitting on the young … you shall not take הָאֵם with the children.”

senses.gloss: mother in Israel: one who cares for a people
senses.definition: A woman who cares for the people as a mother, and a chief city that holds its people as a mother does.

evidence.note: “Until I, Deborah, arose, שַׁקַּמְתִּי אֵם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל”, arose a mother in Israel.
Abel: “You are seeking to kill עִיר וְאֵם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל”, a city and a mother in Israel, “the inheritance of Yahweh”.

senses.gloss: mother: a nation or city as mother of its people
senses.definition: A nation, city or royal house personified as the mother of those born in it: Israel the wife Yahweh sent away for her transgressions, Jerusalem whose mother was a Hittite, Babylon the mother put to shame. The New Testament keeps the figure in the Jerusalem above, the mother of the children of promise, and in Babylon, mother of harlots.

evidence.note: “Where is the writing of divorce of אִמְּכֶם, whom I sent away? … for your transgressions was אִמְּכֶם sent away.”
“Contend בְאִמְּכֶם, contend, for she is not my wife, and I am not her husband.”
“I will destroy אִמֶּךָ”: the nation.
To Jerusalem: “your father the Amorite and אִמֵּךְ a Hittite”.
“כְּאִמָּה בִּתָּהּ”: as the mother, her daughter.
The princes of Israel: “What was אִמְּךָ? A lioness!”
“אִמְּךָ like a vine … planted by the waters.”
To the Chaldeans: “אִמְּכֶם is greatly ashamed”, beside יוֹלַדְתְּכֶם, she who bore you.
“The Jerusalem above is free, which is μήτηρ of us all”; the Peshitta has אֵמַנ, our mother.
“Babylon the great, ἡ μήτηρ of harlots”; Peshitta אֵמָא.
The figure turned to death: Job calls the pit his father and the worm אִמִּי and his sister.

senses.definition: Once, the point where a road divides, as a mother from whom the two ways go out.

evidence.note: “The king of Babylon stands אֶל אֵם הַדֶּרֶךְ, בְּרֹאשׁ שְׁנֵי הַדְּרָכִים”: at the mother of the way, at the head of the two ways.

evidence.locator: Gen.3.20, אֵם → μήτηρ; Gen.2.24, אִמּוֹ → μητέρα; Isa.50.1, אִמְּכֶם → μητρὸς, μητέρα; Hos.2.4, בְאִמְּכֶם → μητέρα

evidence.note: Jesus quotes Gen 2:24: “a man will leave his father and τὴν μητέρα”.
Gen 2:24 again.
Quoting Exo 20:12 and 21:17: honour father and mother; the one speaking evil of father or mother, let him die.
Exo 20:12, “the first commandment with a promise”.
Mic 7:6: a daughter against her mother.
The Jerusalem above, μήτηρ of us all: the figure of Isa 50:1 and Hos 2:4.

parallels.note: Father, paired with mother in honour, teaching, mourning and cursing.
She who bore: the mother named by her bearing.
Sister, beside mother of the worm that is Job’s kin in death.

opposites.note: The barren woman, whom Yahweh makes “the joyful mother of children”.

evidence.note: Isa 54:1, the barren one, quoted of the Jerusalem that is mother (Gal 4:26).

phrases.gloss: mother’s house, where a daughter belongs before marriage
son of (one’s) mother: full brother, the nearest kin

evidence.note: “Benjamin his brother, בֶּן אִמּוֹ”.
The opposite: Sarah the daughter of Abraham’s father, “but not בַת אִמִּי”.

phrases.gloss: mother’s womb: the beginning of a life
and his mother’s name was (at a king’s accession)
the mother of the way: where a road divides

words.summary: Once only, Isa 6:4, in the plural construct אַמּוֹת הַסִּפִּים, the אַמּוֹת of the thresholds that shook at the seraph’s cry: some part of the doorway, posts or sockets or the ground the threshold rests on. The key’s count of 249 is by spelling and belongs to the cubit; this word has one use, and nothing in scripture fixes its sense. Akkadian ammatu “earth, ground” is a possible match; with no cognate of its own sharing a fixed meaning, the root’s other cognates count against it in the evidence table. It may be the cubit word itself, the doorposts as the arms of the door, but no use shows that.

senses.gloss: post or base (?) of the threshold
senses.definition: Some part of the temple doorway, named with the thresholds, which moved when the voice called: the posts, the pivots or the ground beneath.

evidence.note: “וַיָּנֻעוּ אַמּוֹת הַסִּפִּים מִקּוֹל הַקּוֹרֵא”: the אַמּוֹת of the thresholds shook at the voice of the one calling, and the house was filled with smoke.

words.summary: Three times in Hebrew (Gen 25:16; Num 25:15; Psa 117:1), of the tribes of Ishmael and of Midian and of all peoples; much more often in Daniel’s Aramaic. Arabic أُمَّة and Syriac ܐܘܡܬܐ are the same word, and Arabic can call a people أُمّ, mother, too: a people as those born of one mother.

senses.definition: A body of kin under one head, such as the twelve tribes of Ishmael’s sons or a father’s house of Midian, and in the plural the peoples of the earth, set beside the nations.

evidence.note: “These are the sons of Ishmael … twelve princes לְאֻמֹּתָם”, by their tribes.
Zur “רֹאשׁ אֻמּוֹת, a father’s house in Midian”: head of clans, beside בֵּית אָב.
“Praise Yahweh, כָּל גּוֹיִם; extol him, כָּל הָאֻמִּים”: all peoples, beside all nations.
Paul quotes Psa 117:1 of the Gentiles’ hope: “all the λαοί”; the Peshitta has אֵמוָתָֿא.
Quoting Psa 117:1: “praise him, all the λαοί”.

parallels.note: Father’s house, the clan named alongside.

words.summary: The Aramaic of Daniel and Ezra, eight times, nearly always in the formula “peoples, nations and languages” (עַמְמַיָּא אֻמַּיָּא וְלִשָּׁנַיָּא) for all the subjects of an empire, and in Dan 7:14 for all who will serve the son of man. The Peshitta’s ܐܘܡܬܐ in Revelation echoes the same formula.

senses.definition: A people among the peoples of an empire; with עַם and לִשָּׁן, the whole of mankind under one rule.

evidence.note: The herald: “To you it is commanded, עַמְמַיָּא אֻמַּיָּא וְלִשָּׁנַיָּא.”
Singular: “any עַם אֻמָּה וְלִשָּׁן that says anything against the God of Shadrach …”.
Nebuchadnezzar’s letter to all peoples, nations and languages “dwelling in all the earth”.
All peoples, nations and languages trembled before Nebuchadnezzar.
To the son of man is given dominion and a kingdom, “that כֹל עַמְמַיָּא אֻמַיָּא וְלִשָּׁנַיָּא should serve him”.
“The rest of אֻמַּיָּא whom Osnappar exiled and settled in the cities of Samaria.”

phrases.gloss: peoples, nations and languages: all the subjects of a world empire

words.summary: The Aramaic of Daniel and Ezra, four times, always the plural אַמִּין, in the same sense as the Hebrew.

senses.definition: The measure of length, for Nebuchadnezzar’s image and for Cyrus’s decree for the house of God.

evidence.note: The golden image: “its height אַמִּין שִׁתִּין, its width אַמִּין שִׁת”.
The house of God: “its height אַמִּין שִׁתִּין, its width אַמִּין שִׁתִּין”.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܐܡܐ (ʾemmā), in about 83 verses, for μήτηρ: a person’s mother, the mother of Jesus, and by figure the Jerusalem above and Babylon.

senses.definition: A mother; Mary as the mother of Jesus; those who do the Father’s will as his mother; and a city as mother of its people.

evidence.note: Gen 2:24: a man shall leave לַאבֻֿוה_י ולֵאמֵה, his father and his mother.
Exo 20:12: “Honour לַאבֻֿוכֿ ולֵאמָכֿ.”
“Mary אֵמֵה, his mother, was betrothed to Joseph.”
Elizabeth: “that the mother of my Lord should come to me”.
Jesus sees לֵאמֵה at the cross.
“מַנ ה_י אֵמי, who is my mother?”
“Whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister וֵאמי.”
The Jerusalem above “which is אֵמַנ, our mother”.
“Babylon the great, אֵמָא of harlots.”

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܐܡܬܐ “cubit” (SEDRA keeps it apart from the ܐܡܬܐ “handmaid” of the same spelling), in four verses, for πῆχυς.

senses.definition: The measure of length: of a man’s stature and of distance.

evidence.note: “Who can add to his stature אַמתָֿא חדָֿא, one cubit?”
“About מַאתֵֿינ אַמִינ, two hundred cubits.”
“144 אַמִינ by the measure of a man.”

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܐܘܡܬܐ, in ten verses, for λαός and ἔθνος: the word of Psa 117:1 in Rom 15:11, and Daniel’s “peoples, nations and languages” in Revelation.

senses.definition: The peoples of the earth, set beside the nations and languages.

evidence.note: Psa 117:1: “praise him, כֻּלהֵינ אֵמוָתָֿא”, for הָאֻמִּים.
Salvation prepared “before the face of כֻֿלהֵינ אֵמוָתָֿא”.
Bought for God “from every tribe and people וֵאמוָתָֿא”: Daniel’s formula.
Psa 2:1: “the peoples (וֵאמוָתָֿא) imagine vain things”, though the Hebrew there is לְאֻמִּים of another root.

cognates.note: Segert: /ʾumm-/ “mother”, with the plural umht “mothers” and umy “my mother” in the letters to the queen mother of Ugarit.

cognates.gloss: mother; mother-city of a colony; mother-city of a people
cognates.note: Phoenician uses the word of a city as Hebrew does: Kition is the “mother” of a colony, and Tyre and Sidon each “mother of the Sidonians” on their coins, as Abel is “a city and a mother in Israel” (2Sa 20:19).

evidence.locator: p. 57, 'M I, n.f. 1. MOTHER; 2. MOTHER-CITY of a colony; 3. MOTHER-CITY of a people

cognates.gloss: mother, of a human being or of any animal; (verb أَمَمْتُ) I was to him a mother
cognates.note: Lane: “A mother … of a human being and of any animal”, so the same span as אֵם of a woman and of a dam (Exo 22:29). The verb أَمَمْتُهُ “I was to him a mother” is formed from the noun.

cognates.note: One word for the forearm and the measure taken from it, as the Hebrew cubit is “the cubit of a man” (Deu 3:11). Akkadian keeps ammatu and ummu “mother” apart by their vowels.

armep x000040140, ammatu [forearm] N (elbow; forearm; a unit of length)

The Targums’ word, with the plural אַמִּין that Daniel and Ezra use.

evidence.note: “cubit. Targ. Ex. XXV, 10; … Pl. אַמִּין (fr. אַמָּא). Targ. Ezek. XL, 5”.

cognates.note: Wiktionary glosses Ugaritic amt “cubit”; Segert’s glossary gives amt only as “handmaid”, the word of Hebrew אָמָה, so the cubit sense needs checking in DULAT.

cognates.gloss: a nation, people, race, tribe; a man’s people, kinsfolk; a generation; a way of life, religion
cognates.note: Lane: “A nation; a people; a race; a tribe, distinct body, or family … as also أُمٌّ”: Arabic can use the mother word itself for a people, which ties אֻמָּה to אֵם.

cognates.note: Cited from Wiktionary only; not found in Segert’s glossary.

cognates.gloss: main body (of an army or workforce); descendants
cognates.note: A body of people and “descendants”, near the Hebrew “tribe”, but its senses (main army, the lower grindstone) are not the same.
A rare Neo-Babylonian ammatu “earth”, which would make Isa 6:4’s אַמּוֹת the ground or bases of the thresholds; one occurrence in Hebrew cannot confirm it.

doctrine.statement: Job says, “Naked I came from the womb of my mother, and naked I will return there” (Job 1:21), and the Preacher says the same of every man: as he came from his mother’s womb, so he goes, and takes nothing of his toil (Ecc 5:14). The return is to the ground he was taken from: “dust you are, and to dust you will return” (Gen 3:19). Facing death, Job calls the pit his father and the worm his mother and sister (Job 17:14). His hope is set on a later day: his redeemer will stand at the last upon the dust, and from his flesh he will see God (Job 19:25–26). From the verses: a man’s life runs from his mother’s womb to the dust, and death brings him to corruption, not to life elsewhere; Job’s hope is in the flesh, at the redeemer’s coming, which is resurrection.

The sufferer of Psalm 22, whose first words Jesus cried on the cross (Psa 22:2; Mat 27:46), says to Yahweh, “you are the one pulling me out from the womb … from the womb of my mother you have been my God” (Psa 22:10–11), and the servant of Isa 49:1 is called by Yahweh “from the bowels of my mother”. Matthew names “his mother Mary”, found with child from the holy spirit (Mat 1:18); the angel sets “holy spirit” beside “power of the Most High” and says that is why the child will be called Son of God (Luk 1:35); Paul says God sent his Son “born of a woman” (Gal 4:4). From the verses: the Son had a mother and began in her womb; he is God’s Son because God’s power caused his conception, and from the womb Yahweh was his God.

Israel is the mother of her people, put away “for your transgressions” (Isa 50:1) and told “she is not my wife” (Hos 2:4); yet Yahweh asks where her writing of divorce is (Isa 50:1) and promises to betroth her to himself for ever, in righteousness and faithfulness (Hos 2:21–22). Isaiah calls the barren one to sing, for her children will be many (Isa 54:1). Paul applies that verse to “the Jerusalem above”, which “is free, which is mother of us all”, and says believers are, like Isaac, “children of promise” (Gal 4:26–28). John sees the new Jerusalem “coming down out of heaven from God” (Rev 21:2). From the verses: the mother of those in Christ is the Jerusalem God gives in fulfilment of the promise, which comes down to the earth; her children are born by promise, as Isaac was.

Nebuchadnezzar commands “peoples, nations and languages” to bow to his image (Dan 3:4), and they tremble before him (Dan 5:19). In Daniel’s vision the same whole of mankind is given to another: to the son of man is given dominion and a kingdom, that “all peoples, nations and languages should serve him”, a dominion that will not pass away (Dan 7:14), and the kingdom “under all the heavens” is given to the people of the saints of the Most High (Dan 7:27). Revelation takes up the formula: the Lamb has bought for God men “from every tribe and people and nation” and made them kings and priests, and “they will reign on the earth” (Rev 5:9–10). From the verses: the kingdom of God replaces the kingdoms of men over the same nations, under heaven and on the earth, with Christ and his saints ruling it.

The ark was 300 cubits long, fifty wide and thirty high (Gen 6:15). The waters rose until “all the high mountains that were under the entire heavens were covered”, and stood fifteen cubits above them (Gen 7:19–20); every living thing on the face of the ground was wiped away, and only Noah and those with him in the ark were left (Gen 7:23). Jesus says the flood came “and took them all” (Mat 24:39), and Peter that “the world of that time was flooded with water and perished” (2Pe 3:6). From the verses: the flood covered every high mountain under the whole heaven to a measured depth, and was over all the earth.

note: Root key אממ: the database files אֵם (a.dx.ab), אַמָּה (a.dx.ad, a.dx.ae) and אֻמָּה (a.dx.ag) under BDB’s אמם, and word_info gives their tokens the root אממ, so the entry takes that key; im.json has root אמ for the particle אִם (a.du.af, filed under אלצ), and the two do not collide. Biblical Aramaic אַמָּה (xa.ar.ac) and אֻמָּה (xa.ar.ad) are keyed under root אמה and carry that as their own root; Hebrew אָמָה “maidservant” (a.dv.ab) is also keyed אמה, so when it gets an entry (with Peshitta ܐܡܬܐ handmaid, SEDRA lexeme 174, and Ugaritic/Phoenician/Sabaean ʾmt) the root אמה will be claimed twice and the lookup by root (first id) must be checked. The Syriac words are given no root: SEDRA root ܐܡ (root 118/127) is אמ, which would claim the particle אִם’s root for this entry. Peshitta words: SEDRA lexeme 159 ܐܡܐ mother (83 verses), 173 ܐܡܬܐ cubit (Mat 6:27; Luk 12:25; Jhn 21:8; Rev 21:17), 158 ܐܘܡܬܐ nation (10 verses); the Syriac lemma for 158 is SEDRA’s unpointed lexeme, as no singular occurs in the New Testament. Left out: a.dx.af (אַמָּה, hill of Ammah, 2Sa 2:24) and a.dx.ah (אֲמָם, Jos 15:26), places; a.dx.ac (מֶתֶג הָאַמָּה, 2Sa 8:1), keyed under מתג; a.du.ag and a.du.ah, cross-references with no tokens; אָמָה “maidservant” (a.dv.ab), another key and root, whose cognates (Akkadian amtu, Arabic ʾama, Ge'ez ʾamat) are ʾmt-, not ʾmm. No personal names are formed from this root. μήτηρ is not recorded as a loan: Thayer sets Hebrew אם beside it but derives it from an Indo-European base. Whether אַמָּה “cubit” shares a base with אֵם and אֻמָּה is open; Akkadian ammatu and ummu differ in vowel, and Biella files Sabaean ʾm “mother” and ʾmt “cubit” as separate roots ('MM I, II). Leads not followed: Ge'ez ʾemmat “cubit” (Biella’s cross-reference; Dillmann not checked); DULAT for Ugaritic amt “cubit” and umt “clan”; CAD for ammatu “earth” (Isa 6:4); Payne Smith for ܐܡܐ and ܐܘܡܬܐ; Lane for any Arabic use of the root for a measure. Open: (1) Jer 51:13 אַמַּת בִּצְעֵךְ, read here as “the measure of your cutting off”; (2) Isa 6:4 אַמּוֹת: posts or bases.
